---
title: "Where next?"
---

All free unless marked.

## New to R and GIS {#new-to-both}

- [*R for Data Science*](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/): start with "Whole game"
- Full [Crime Mapping in R workbook](https://maczokni.github.io/crime_mapping_textbook/): nine labs, from install to spatial regression
- [*Crime Mapping and Spatial Data Analysis using R*](https://maczokni.github.io/crime_mapping/) (Medina & Solymosi, 2023)
- [UK Data Service training](https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/learning-hub/): free webinars, including crime mapping in R

## Know R {#know-r}

- [*Geocomputation with R*](https://r.geocompx.org/): `sf`, `terra`, spatial operations
- [*Spatial Data Science*](https://r-spatial.org/book/) (Pebesma & Bivand): theory, by the `sf`/`spdep` authors
- [*Spatial Statistics for Data Science*](https://www.paulamoraga.com/book-spatial/) (Moraga)
- Packages: `tmap` (thematic maps), `leaflet` (web maps), `spatstat` (point patterns, KDE), `spatialreg` (spatial regression), `sfdep`

## Know GIS {#know-gis}

- [`sf` cheat sheet](https://github.com/rstudio/cheatsheets/blob/main/sf.pdf): GIS operations → R functions
- [Data Carpentry: geospatial R](https://datacarpentry.github.io/r-raster-vector-geospatial/)
- QGIS can run R scripts (Processing R Provider plugin)
- What R adds: **reproducibility**. Every choice is written down.

## Practitioners {#practitioners}

- Chainey & Ratcliffe (2005) *GIS and Crime Mapping*. Wiley. (Not free.)
- Module chapters: [spatial operations](https://maczokni.github.io/crime_mapping_textbook/performing-spatial-operations-in-r.html), [hot spots / KDE](https://maczokni.github.io/crime_mapping_textbook/studying-spatial-point-patterns.html)
- When presenting a map, report the **unit, denominator, classification and time window**

## Open data

- Crime: [data.police.uk](https://data.police.uk/)
- Census: [nomis](https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/sources/census_2021)
- Boundaries: [ONS Open Geography Portal](https://geoportal.statistics.gov.uk/)
- Streets and amenities: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/) (R package `osmdata`)

## Readings from today

- Anselin (1995) [LISA](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-4632.1995.tb00338.x). *Geographical Analysis*
- Brantingham & Brantingham (1995) [Criminality of place](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02242925). *Eur J Crim Policy Res*
- Gerell (2017) [Smallest is better?](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10940-016-9297-6) *J Quant Criminol*
- Openshaw (1984) *The Modifiable Areal Unit Problem*. CATMOG 38
- Rengert & Lockwood (2009) [Geographical units of analysis](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-09688-9_5). In *Putting Crime in its Place*
- Tompson et al. (2015) [UK open crime data: accuracy](https://doi.org/10.1080/15230406.2014.972456). *Cartogr Geogr Inf Sci*
- Weisburd (2015) [The law of crime concentration](https://doi.org/10.1111/1745-9125.12070). *Criminology*
